title: Text + tabular (binary)
description: A yes or no from free text and the structured fields that come with it.
metrics: Recall at the review budget (the share of cases found when the team reviews its budget)
question: Which decisions does DCLab reach on a text + tabular (binary) problem (A yes or no from free text and the structured fields that come with it), and do they hold?
hypothesis: Each decision a careful data scientist reaches on this kind of problem holds on every seed of the kind's replica.
setup_summary: The text + tabular (binary) kind's replica on seeds 0, 1, 2, brought as a person would; the five stages of the engine solve it, and each decision is checked on the finished run. No model is called.

decisions.decision: `shop_reply` is kept out of the model (written after the review)

a text recipe is chosen over the structured fields alone
the chosen recipe beats the structured fields by 0.1 training-CV
the holdout ROC-AUC is at least 0.8
no copy of the label is left (holdout ROC-AUC below 0.99)
the baselines the kind declares are the ones the final stage computes

claims.statement: Text + tabular (binary): on 3 of 3 seeds every decision held (95% interval over seeds [0.439, 1.0]); 24 of 24 decision checks held.
limitations: Invented replicas with planted traps, three seeds: what the kind decides, not how well it does on real data.
Checks on one seed share its data, so they are not independent: the interval over seeds is the honest one.
